# PnL {#sec-pnl}

*This section covers* the bottom line — wrapping a complete engine in a profit model. Two views of the same economics:

- **@sec-pnl-consolidated** — the `pnl`: one consolidated net group (consideration / obligation / margin), the summary card.
- **@sec-pnl-walk** — the `xpnl`: the step-by-step walk gross → each cession → Total, showing how the consolidated view is built.

Both inherit premium from the wrapped book and read scenario (κ) columns beside the marginal (P) percentiles.


```{python}
#| echo: true
from aggregate import build, qd, __version__ as v
from greater_tables import GT, Fabricator, __version__ as vgt
print(v, vgt)
import aggregate.style
aggregate.style.use()
from aggregate.plots import make_grid
%config InlineBackend.figure_format = 'svg'
from aggregate.utilities import silence_warnings
silence_warnings()
```


## PNL walk
Make gross

```{python}
g = build('''
agg Gross as "Gross Book"
    20000 loss
    5000 xs 0
    sev lognorm 100 cv 3
    mixed gamma 0.1
''')
qd(g)
```

Net Occ ... use xpnl, run, see losses, then calibrate premiums

```{python}
n = build('''
xpnl NO as "Occ Analysis"
    30000 premium as "GWP"
    less
    agg Subject as "Gross"
        20000 loss
        5000 xs 0
        sev lognorm 100 cv 3
        occurrence net of
            50% po 500 xs 500 and
            90% po 1000 xs 1000 and
            95% po 3000 xs 2000
        mixed gamma 0.1
    peel bottom-up
''')
qd(n)
```

Now add the premiums.

```{python}
n1 = build('''
xpnl NO as "Occ Analysis"
    30000 premium as "GWP"
    less
    agg Subject as "Gross"
        20000 loss
        5000 xs 0
        sev lognorm 100 cv 3
        occurrence net of
            50% po 500 xs 500 deposit 2500 and
            90% po 1000 xs 1000 deposit 2200 and
            95% po 3000 xs 2000 deposit 1000
        mixed gamma 0.1
    peel bottom-up
''')
qd(n1)
```

Look at the net distribution to assess aggregate program options. Look at quantiles

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
ps = np.linspace(.8, .99, 20)
df = pd.DataFrame({'p': ps, 'Quantile': n1.engine.q(ps)})
print(GT(df, float_format=2))
```

Next, add an agg program. Same process, add without premium, assess, then add premium. We'll do in one step. Add labels

```{python}
n2 = build('''
xpnl NO as "Re Analysis"
    30000 premium as "GWP"
    less
    agg Subject as "Gross"
        20000 loss
        5000 xs 0
        sev lognorm 100 cv 3
        occurrence net of
            50% po 500 xs 500 deposit 2500 as "500x500"and
            90% po 1000 xs 1000 deposit 2200 as "1x1" and
            95% po 3000 xs 2000 deposit 1000 as "3x2"
        mixed gamma 0.1
        aggregate net of
            60% po 1000 xs 20000 deposit 250 as "Agg 1x20" and
            90% po 2000 xs 22000 deposit 100 as "Agg 2x22"
    peel bottom-up
''')
# trim answer
cols = ['EX', 'SD', 'CV', 'P99']
bit = n2.summary_df[cols]
print(GT(bit))
```

Look at just the margin progression.

```{python}
bit2 = bit.xs('Margin', axis=0, level='Side')
print(GT(bit2, caption='Margin by Step'))
```

Try a quota share instead of the aggregate program. Swing rated with cede. Start without the occ program. Look gross first

```{python}
df = pd.DataFrame({'p': ps, 'Quantile': g.q(ps)})
print(GT(df, float_format=2, caption='Gross Percentiles'))
```

Try limited quota share, to 95th percentile - note Python injection.

```{python}
limit = g.q(0.95)
n2 = build(f'''
xpnl NO as "Re2 Analysis"
    30000 premium as "GWP"
    less
    agg Subject as "Gross"
        20000 loss
        5000 xs 0
        sev lognorm 100 cv 3
        mixed gamma 0.1
        aggregate net of
            100% po {limit} xs 0
                deposit 30000 slide 20% at 80% and 10% at 90%
                as "Slide"
    less
    8000 fixed expense as "Gen&Acq"
    # peel bottom-up
''')
# trim answer
cols = ['EX', 'SD', 'CV', 'κ01', 'κ50', 'κ99']
bit = n2.stats_df[cols]
print(GT(bit, caption=f"QS, limit {limit:,.0f}"))
```
